label: M5 fsincos read the wrong way round: the cosine into [eax] and the sine into [edx]. fsincos leaves st0 = cos, so the FIRST fstp (0x102d7c66, through edx, the slot the entry addressed first) is the cosine. Every field changes, and so does which of the two scratch slots holds which

label: M6 the three movsd copy forward whatever the direction flag says. With DF set the entry writes the second and third words onto the saved esi and edi and reads never-initialised slots for ky and kz, so the pops hand back axis floats and the matrix is built from the stack's own bytes - the harness fuzzes df, so this is not a hypothetical
find: const int step = g->df ? -4 : 4; /* the three movsd walk esi AND edi by +4, or by -4 with DF set */

label: M7 the (2,2) field squares the MEMORY slot instead of the register kz the entry has carried since 0x102d7c99. Only the aliased-object state can see it: there, the (1,2) store at 0x102d7cfd has overwritten [ebp-0x14] long before 0x102d7d1c

M8 the addition's NaN rule turned back to st(0). Identical on every finite pair and on every single-NaN pair, which is exactly why this unit needs the two-NaN axis state: without it a caller-visible difference - the payload in +0x18 and +0x20 - would be unguarded

M9 the memory-form multiply written with the loaded operand first. MISSED, and recorded rather than fixed: cowdiff cannot tell the two spellings apart, so which operand a C multiplication writes first is not a property of this unit at all - MSVC chooses the destination register and textual order does not reach it (build/probe_nan_codegen.c shows the same for both orders of the addition). What the memory/register SPLIT buys is transcription fidelity - the entry has two forms and they are two different instructions - and the only place where a NaN rule had to be STATED is the addition (M8)
